clue.text: Earthy jazz style Y-Yank backs, endlessly cheered inside

indicators.note: the cheering word is placed inside the other piece rather than beside it
something that backs goes in reverse, so the yanking letters are read from the end

parts.note: a yank is a tug; the hyphenated prefix must be read as a T for the letters to work

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the cheering word is dropped

parts.note: bucked up, made cheerful

explanation.surface: A music critic describes a raw jazz style with some odd talk of yanking and cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: As transcribed the clue reads 'Y-Yank', but the letters only work as a T-tug: a yank is a tug, with a T prefixed, and that is what turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutbucket is a raw, unpolished, earthy style of jazz or blues, named after the bucket used as a makeshift instrument.

clue.text: Fatuous fellow from Ohio in Republican party

indicators.note: in places one piece within the party's letters

parts.note: GOP, Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party
O is the postal abbreviation for Ohio's first letter

explanation.surface: A silly man from Ohio in the Republican Party.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes into GOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A goop is a foolish, fatuous person, a slang term from early twentieth-century America.

clue.text: One localized conflict that is unexpected for old poet

parts.note: 'un is dialect for one, as in 'a good 'un'
a war is a conflict
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A local war that broke out without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For old poet' marks a word of Spenser's.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwarie is Spenser's spelling of unwary in an old sense, unforeseen or happening without warning.

clue.text: Old coin revealed when my trash is recycled

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and reformed, so these letters are remade in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Recycling the rubbish turns up an ancient coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrymsa was an early Anglo-Saxon gold coin, later silver, of the seventh century.

clue.text: Dig up short note misplaced in air-trap

indicators.note: in shows where the moved letters go back, within the trap word
misplaced means moved out of its proper position, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: a U-bend in a drain traps water, sealing out the air and smells
NB, nota bene, is a short note of warning

explanation.surface: A plumber digs out a pipe after a note was left in the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: In U-BEND the N and B swap round to sit straight after the U.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbed is to take something out of its bed, as a gardener lifts bulbs, so it can mean dig up.

clue.text: Ticker reset when chicken's put in cooker

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so the chicken word sits within the other letters
something reset is put back together differently, so these letters change their order

parts.note: taken as written
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: A cook resets the oven timer when the chicken goes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticker' sounds like the clock on the oven; it is just letters to rearrange around HEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchener is an old-fashioned kitchen range, the cast-iron stove used for cooking.

clue.text: Mutiny in the form of riot tar stirred up — and where?

indicators.note: stirred-up contents are mixed around, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a ship is where a mutiny traditionally happens

explanation.surface: A sailor stirs up a riot on board, and someone asks where.
explanation.walkthrough: A riot by a tar, a sailor, is mutiny, and 'and where?' answers itself with the place it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Traitorship is the state of being a traitor, and a mutiny is treachery against those in command.

clue.text: Former saying, what Sam came out with briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so only the start of the work's name is kept

parts.note: Samuel Johnson published his famous Dictionary in 1755

explanation.surface: An old saying that someone called Sam once came out with.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam is Dr Samuel Johnson; dict is also the usual short form of dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Dict is an obsolete noun for a saying or pronouncement, related to dictum.

clue.text: Tree down under, reverse of healthy after start of blight

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter

indicators.note: the reverse of a word reads it from end to beginning

parts.note: hale means healthy

explanation.surface: An Australian tree recovers its health after an attack of blight.
explanation.walkthrough: Down under means Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The belah is an Australian casuarina, a tree with drooping jointed branches.

clue.text: Wife, three-quarters fidgety, right? Backbreaker may floor one

indicators.note: three-quarters means only that share of the word is kept, the last part dropped

parts.note: w is the abbreviation for wife
restless means fidgety
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A fidgety wife with a bad back worries a heavy load may floor her.
explanation.walkthrough: Six of the eight letters of RESTLESS are three-quarters. A backbreaker is a wrestling throw across the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler is a grappler in the ring who could be thrown to the mat by the move called a backbreaker.

clue.text: Acceptable performer available (6, two words)

parts.note: on as in 'that's not on': acceptable
a hand is a worker or performer, as in 'a dab hand'

explanation.surface: A casting agent notes that a decent performer is free to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket at the end is the source's way of giving the enumeration, two words of six letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on hand is close by and ready for use, which is the everyday sense of available.

clue.text: Eastern tree I found restricted by a tabu, rudimentary

indicators.note: restricted by means hemmed in on both sides, so these pieces sit inside the ban

parts.note: taken as written
a tabu, or taboo, is a ban
E is the abbreviation for eastern
a cedar is a coniferous tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree from the East held back by a primitive taboo.
explanation.walkthrough: Tabu is an older spelling of taboo, and a taboo is a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Abecedarian means relating to the alphabet, hence elementary, at the level of a beginner learning ABC.

clue.text: Like a stronger martini in club? Not very

indicators.note: 'not' tells the solver to remove whatever 'very' stands for from the golf word

parts.note: a driver is a golf club
v is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A drinker at the club bar asks for a stiffer martini and is told not really.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' sits in the bar scene, but it is the golf club DRIVER; take out V and DRIER is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry martini has little vermouth, so a stronger, more gin-heavy one is described as drier.

clue.text: Compass case, part to confront with measure of bits missing

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so this unit's letter is taken out of the confronting word

parts.note: to tackle a problem is to confront it
K, kilo, as in kilobits, measures quantities of data bits

explanation.surface: A computing instruction about tackling a component when part of the data has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: BIT plus TACKLE without its K gives BITTACLE, the older form of binnacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bittacle, an old variant of binnacle, is the housing on a ship's deck that holds the compass.

clue.text: Person often following 'account', always penned by number one?

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed by it, as if fenced in a pen

parts.note: number one is nursery slang for urinating, and the question mark flags it
ay, or aye, is an old and Scottish word for always

explanation.surface: Someone always written about by the top person in a company's accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like the boss, but it is childish toilet slang. On a British cheque, 'account payee' between crossed lines means only the named person can bank it.
explanation.definitionFit: On a cheque marked 'account payee' the word payee follows 'account'; the payee is the person who receives the money.

clue.text: An army's quota I cut in endless tally?

indicators.note: in places the reduced quota within the shortened tally
cut means removed, so the stated letter is taken out of the quota word

parts.note: a tally stick was a notched stick used for keeping count

indicators.note: endless means without its last letter, so the tally word loses its final letter

parts.note: a ration is an allotted quota
taken as written, to be cut

explanation.surface: An army totting up its share of supplies on a tally stick.
explanation.walkthrough: RATION without I is RATON, which goes into STIC (stick without its K).
explanation.definitionFit: Stratonic, from Greek stratos, an army, means belonging to an army, so it can replace 'an army's'.

clue.text: Placed in vessel it lives

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so one piece sits within the vessel word

parts.note: vas is the Latin word for a vessel, used for ducts in anatomy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something placed in a container is said to live there.
explanation.walkthrough: Vitas is an anglicised plural of the Latin vita; the dictionary also gives vitae.
explanation.definitionFit: A vita is a life or a short biography, and Chambers allows vitas as its plural, so the word means lives.

clue.text: Tribe met in the wars turn hostile

indicators.note: something in the wars is battered and knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two tribes meet in battle and become enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: In the wars is a British idiom for being bruised or battered.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter is to fill with resentment, making someone turn hostile.

clue.text: New brood, kept inside dry once covered in straw?

indicators.note: kept inside means held within, so the brood word goes between the letters for dry

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol: dry
a hatch is a brood of newly hatched chicks

explanation.surface: Newly hatched birds kept dry in a straw-lined nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' belongs to the definition: it marks an old spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatcht is an archaic form of thatched, meaning roofed with straw or reeds.

clue.text: What can bore well, or screw (though old)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large auger used for boring wells
second meaning: a stingy person, for which screw is old slang

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' and 'screw' suggest tools throughout, but only the first half is a tool; a screw is also slang for a skinflint.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is both a well-boring auger in Chambers and a hoarder of money, someone mean enough to be called a screw.

clue.text: Transferring old basin taken back, with second installed

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so the second word goes within the basin word
taken back means carried in the opposite direction, so the basin word is read right to left

parts.note: a laver is an old word for a washing basin
mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Moving house, an old washbasin is taken back and a new part fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo, as in 'half a mo', is the usual crossword second.
explanation.definitionFit: Removal is the act of moving something from one place to another, so it can stand for transferring as a noun.

clue.text: Palm Monsieur put in his wine as 'food factor'

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so the palm and Monsieur letters go inside the wine

parts.note: vin is the Frenchman's word for wine, his because Monsieur is French
the ita is a South American palm tree
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman pours palm wine as a health supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm' looks like a hand; it is the ita palm.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamins were first called accessory food factors, the trace nutrients a diet needs for health.

clue.text: Deadly poison I included in a short story

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something included in another is placed within it

parts.note: a conte is a short story, especially a French one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deadly poison features in a short mystery story.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, also called monkshood or wolfsbane, is a plant whose extract is a lethal poison.

clue.text: Strangely mad in the head, one had to pray for others

definitions.text: one had to pray for others

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for head

parts.note: bean is slang for the head

indicators.note: something done strangely is done oddly, so these letters come out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who seems a little touched in the head was once paid to pray for others.
explanation.walkthrough: DMA, the shuffled MAD, goes into BEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadman, or beadsman, was someone paid or endowed to say prayers for a benefactor, counting them on beads.

clue.text: Good grain — did the first go to market?

definitions.text: did the first go to market?

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A farmer with fine grain wonders whether the first lot went to market.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy went to market', the first of the toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A grice is a young pig, and in the rhyme the first little piggy is the one that goes to market.

clue.text: Foreign prince having entered temple, with time inside

parts.note: having entered, you are in

indicators.note: inside means within, so the letter for time sits in the temple word

parts.note: a fane is a temple
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A visiting prince goes into a temple and spends some time there.
explanation.walkthrough: Fane is a poetic word for a temple, much used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An infante is a son of the king of Spain or Portugal other than the heir, so a foreign prince.

clue.text: Extract of bromine also strengthens

indicators.note: an extract is drawn out of a larger body, so the letters are taken from inside the following words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A chemist notes that bromine extract makes things stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: To neal is an old form of anneal, to toughen metal or glass by heating and slow cooling.

clue.text: Spectator is fancily dressed — showing –– esprit perhaps

definitions.text: Spectator is fancily dressed — showing –– esprit perhaps

indicators.note: fancy dress turns someone into something else, so the letters are reworked
a minus sign means subtract, so the following letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be subtracted

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed racegoer shows off their wit.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: remove the letters of ESPRIT from SPECTATOR IS and rearrange the rest. The whole clue describes the scene, so it is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Ascot is the English race meeting famous for spectators in elaborate hats and formal dress.

clue.text: Have a go at containing flow of water with waterworks fully active

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the water word goes inside the attempt word

parts.note: to try is to have a go at
ea is a dialect word for a river or stream

explanation.definitionFit: Someone teary is close to crying, and turning on the waterworks is a jokey idiom for shedding tears.

clue.text: Acres typical of lord, landed

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for acres
lit means drunk, and 'drunk as a lord' is the idiom

explanation.surface: Broad acres are typical of a landed lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landed' suggests a lord's estates; here it is the past tense of land, as a bird does.
explanation.definitionFit: Alit is a past tense of alight, to come down and settle, so it means landed.

clue.text: Dynasty has briefly to hold back

parts.note: has is cut to 's, as in 'she's got'
to hang back is to hold back

explanation.surface: A ruling house that tends to stay in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'S plus HANG, the verb from 'hang back', gives SHANG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shang were the early Chinese dynasty that ruled the Yellow River valley in the second millennium BC.

clue.text: Moved on,w switching parts of advantage

indicators.note: switching parts means its two halves trade places

a stray letter in this copy of the clue, giving nothing

clue.text: I act misguidedly bagging cat as reprisal ?

parts.note: taken as written
a lion is a big cat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' is a big cat, not a domestic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Talionic relates to the lex talionis, the law of retaliation, an eye for an eye, so it describes punishment as reprisal.

clue.text: As a devotee of Charles, I'll be gripped by stylish vigour

indicators.note: to be gripped by something is to be held inside it

parts.note: elan is flair and vigour
I, with the 'll only there to make the sentence run

explanation.surface: A royalist loyal to King Charles promises to be carried along by the cause's dash and vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charles' suggests a king, but it is the essayist Charles Lamb, who wrote as Elia. I goes inside ELAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Elian means in the manner of Elia, Charles Lamb's pen name, so an Elian is a devotee of his essays.

clue.text: The poodle is poorly? Maybe he, put to sleep thus, old

indicators.note: something in poor shape is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be taken away
taken as written, to be taken away

explanation.surface: A sick old dog may have to be put down, which is what the owner fears.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: some letters are taken away from 'The poodle is' before the rest are rearranged. The minus signs between the pieces seem to have been lost in this transcription.
explanation.definitionFit: Sopite is an obsolete verb meaning to lull or put to sleep, from Latin sopire.

clue.text: I intend getting drunk around company reeking of fags?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the company letters are enclosed
drunk letters stagger out of their order, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A drinker plans to get drunk among smokers in a smelly pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Fags is British slang for cigarettes. The rearranged I INTEND wraps CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nicotined is stained or tainted with nicotine, the drug in cigarettes, so it reeks of them.
